notes: Translations: NIV for most verses because it reads plainly aloud; ESV where it reads better (the sparrow, and Mark 1:13 in beat 6); the Douay-Rheims only for the basilisk, because it is the English of the Latin Bible Moretto knew.
Every verse was copied from the published text on BibleGateway. Verses are trimmed to the phrase that matters; where one starts mid-verse its first letter is capitalized.
The story lines try not to repeat the verses. The verse carries the meaning.
Unfold beat titles are now wall titles, not the working names from the design document.
Nothing here is final. Every line stays marked draft until you approve it.

subjects.title: Christ
subjects.short: Forty days without food. He sits with his chin in his hand.

more.story: Israel spent forty years in the wilderness, complaining about bread. When Satan tells the hungry Jesus to make some, he answers from Deuteronomy.

verses.text: Man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.

subjects.note: The two verses nearly match on purpose: Jesus is quoting Deuteronomy word for word.

subjects.title: The Angels
subjects.short: Two angels come down from the upper right to care for him.

more.story: Elijah ran into the wilderness and lay down to die. An angel woke him and fed him, and he walked forty days on that food.

verses.text: All at once an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended him.

subjects.title: The Basilisk
subjects.short: A small winged serpent, half hidden near the center. It may be a basilisk.

more.story: The Latin Bible Moretto knew names a basilisk in the psalm that Satan quotes to Jesus here in the wilderness.

verses.text: Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.

subjects.note: Psalm 90:13 is the Latin Bible's numbering; modern Bibles call it 91:13. The Met does not name the creature, so the short line says “may be”.

subjects.title: The Lion
subjects.short: A lion lies at the lower right, half outside the picture.

more.story: Here the lion lies calm, close to Christ. In the Bible the lion is first Judah’s sign, then a name for Jesus.

verses.text: You are a lion’s cub, Judah… Like a lion he crouches and lies down.
See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed.

subjects.note: The Genesis line uses one ellipsis to join two phrases of the same verse.

subjects.title: The Stag
subjects.short: A stag crosses the slope at the left.

more.story: A deer searching for water was the psalmist’s picture of a soul that longs for God.

verses.text: As the deer pants for streams of water, so my soul pants for you, my God.
Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.

subjects.title: The Fox
subjects.short: A fox rests a few steps from the serpent.

more.story: Mark says only that Jesus was with the wild animals. Moretto filled the slope with them, the fox among them.

verses.text: Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for herself
Foxes have dens and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay his head.

subjects.note: The weakest pairing: creatures with homes, and Jesus without one. Cut the Psalm if it feels forced.

subjects.title: The Bear
subjects.short: A dark bear lies in the grass, as quiet as everything else.

more.story: Isaiah described a coming king whose peace would reach even the wild animals.

verses.text: The cow will feed with the bear, their young will lie down together
He was with the wild animals.

subjects.title: The Missing Picture
subjects.short: Faint cherubs at the left edge, where the original canvas was cut down.

more.story: Moretto’s painting once continued past this edge, with other scenes from Christ’s life.

verses.text: Jesus did many other things as well.

subjects.note: Only one verse here, from the New Testament. I could not find an Old Testament pairing that did not feel forced.

beats.title: In the Beginning
beats.short: God brings the animals to the first man, and he names them.

more.story: Genesis begins in a garden where the first man lives among the animals without fear.

verses.text: He brought them to the man to see what he would name them

beats.title: The Promise
beats.short: After the fall, God tells the serpent that its head will be crushed.

more.story: Christians have long read this as the first promise of Christ.

verses.text: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet.

beats.title: Forty Years
beats.short: Israel wandered in the wilderness for forty years.

more.story: Each morning God gave them manna, enough for that day.

verses.text: Remember how the LORD your God led you all the way in the wilderness these forty years

beats.title: Forty Days
beats.short: Jesus goes into the same wilderness for forty days.

more.story: Hungry and tempted, he answers Satan three times with words from Deuteronomy.

verses.text: Man does not live on bread alone but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.

beats.title: Fed in the Wilderness
beats.short: An angel once fed the prophet Elijah in the wilderness.

more.story: When the temptations are over, angels come and care for Jesus.

verses.text: All at once an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
Then the devil left him, and angels came and attended him.

beats.title: The Peaceable Kingdom
beats.short: Isaiah saw a peace that would reach even the wild animals.

more.story: Moretto painted the hunters and the hunted lying still together around Christ.

verses.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, the leopard will lie down with the goat
And he was with the wild animals, and the angels were ministering to him.

beats.title: The Lion and the Serpent
beats.short: Satan quoted Psalm 91 to Jesus. He stopped just before the verse about the lion.

more.story: Later Jesus tells his followers they will trample snakes, an echo of the same psalm.

verses.text: You will tread on the lion and the cobra; you will trample the great lion and the serpent.
I have given you authority to trample on snakes and scorpions

beats.note: Satan quotes Psalm 91:11–12 in Matthew 4:6; verse 13 is the next line. Here the modern number (91) is used, since this beat quotes the NIV.

beats.title: The Rest of the Story
beats.short: This canvas was cut from a larger painting of Christ’s life.

more.story: What remains shows Jesus alone and hungry, at peace among the animals.

verses.text: Jesus did many other things as well.
